content.comment_body: I'm unable to open the files I create myself, but I can access example files downloaded from [company_name]'s website. My account has administrator rights, and the files aren't marked as read-only. Their location doesn't seem to affect this issue either. The file extension is .lsc, without any ladder inputs. I'm running Windows 7 64-bit. Any suggestions?

Here's what I tried: I uninstalled Java from my computer. Although the application claims to use Java, it still functioned without it—unexpected. When opening the file with Windows File Explorer, I receive an error, but if I use the open menu within the application itself, it loads correctly. This seems like an issue with the application. Reinstalling Java made no difference. Restarting the system also didn't help. So the problem is mostly resolved by using the application to open files, but the root cause persists.
Does the file name contain spaces or special characters?

analysis.insight_summary: Users are encountering difficulties opening their own .lsc files with the [product_name] demo version on Windows 7 64-bit. While example files from [company_name]'s website open without problems, user-created and saved files show errors if accessed directly through Windows Explorer; however, these files open correctly when accessed via the application's open menu. Removing and reinstalling Java has no effect on the issue, suggesting it is related to the application's integration with Windows and file association settings.
analysis.user_expectations: Users expect to be able to reliably open their saved project files, regardless of whether they use Windows Explorer or the application's internal open menu.
